name.text: Scatterplot — most appropriate linear model (randomised MCQ)

questiontext.text:
The scatterplot below shows a set of data points.

[[jsxgraph width="520px" height="480px"]] var PX=[1,2,3,4,5,6]; var PY=[{#y1#},{#y2#},{#y3#},{#y4#},{#y5#},{#y6#}]; var XMAX=7, YMAX={#float(ymaxwin)#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.6, YMAX, XMAX, -2], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[XMAX-0.1, -0.9, 'x'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:14,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.12, YMAX-0.4, 'y'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:14,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); for (var i=0;i<6;i++){ brd.create('point',[PX[i],PY[i]],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3}); } [[/jsxgraph]]

Which of the following equations is the most appropriate linear model for the data shown in the scatterplot?

[[input:ansModel]] [[validation:ansModel]] [[feedback:prtModel]]

generalfeedback.text:
Read two things from the scatterplot.

  • Direction (sign of the slope). The points are [[ if test="is(sgn=1)" ]] rising, so the slope is positive. [[ else ]] falling, so the slope is negative. [[/ if ]]
  • Intercept vs slope. The \(y\)-intercept (where the line meets the \(y\)-axis) is about \({@c@}\); the line changes by about \({@sm@}\) in \(y\) for each step of \(1\) in \(x\), so the slope has magnitude \({@sm@}\).

So the most appropriate model is {#correctdisp#}: the constant is the intercept and the coefficient of \(x\) is the slope. Swapping them (using \({@sm@}\) as the intercept) or using the wrong sign gives the distractors.

[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="440px"]] var PX=[1,2,3,4,5,6]; var PY=[{#y1#},{#y2#},{#y3#},{#y4#},{#y5#},{#y6#}]; var C={#c#}, M={#float(m)#}, XMAX=7, YMAX={#float(ymaxwin)#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.6, YMAX, XMAX, -2], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[XMAX-0.1, -0.9, 'x'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.12, YMAX-0.4, 'y'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('functiongraph',[function(x){ return C + M*x; }, 0, XMAX-0.3],{strokeColor:'#cc0000', strokeWidth:2, highlight:false}); for (var i=0;i<6;i++){ brd.create('point',[PX[i],PY[i]],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3}); } brd.create('point',[0,C],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#cc0000',size:3}); [[/jsxgraph]]

truefeedback.text: You have the right numbers, but check the direction of the trend: the points are [[ if test="is(sgn=1)" ]] rising, so the slope should be positive [[ else ]] falling, so the slope should be negative [[/ if ]].

falsefeedback.text: You have swapped the intercept and the slope. The \(y\)-intercept (where the line crosses the \(y\)-axis) is the constant term, and the slope (the smaller number here) multiplies \(x\).
